input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The exception-message predicate requires the regular expression to match the entire exception message.
- failure path: Given an exception message with a matching prefix followed by additional diagnostic text, the retry condition returns false and Tenacity propagates the exception without retrying.

Reviewer finding
- description: Changing `self.match.match(...)` to `self.match.fullmatch(...)` silently changes matching semantics: a pattern that previously matched a prefix of the exception string now requires the entire string to match.
- rationale: Trigger: retry_if_exception_message(match="Connection") and an exception with str "Connection refused". The old re.match code returned True, so the retry happened. With fullmatch the check returns False, so the retry predicate no longer fires and the exception is not retried. Users who relied on prefix/partial matching get silently different retry behavior with no error raised.
critique: The finding identifies the switch to fullmatch, which requires the whole exception message to match. As a result, a message with a matching prefix plus extra text no longer triggers a retry. This is the same mechanism and failure path as the labeled defect.
